distractors.reason: We don't say 'depend from'. 'Depend' is always followed by 'on' in this meaning.
We don't say 'depend of'. The correct preposition is 'on'.
We don't say 'depend with'. The fixed partner of 'depend' is 'on'.

example_sentence: Our picnic depended ___ the weather, so we checked the forecast.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden traducir 'depender de' de forma literal y decir 'depend from' o 'depend of'. En inglés, el verbo 'depend' siempre va con 'on'.
explanation: In English, 'depend' takes 'on' when it means that something is controlled by or based on another thing. Use it to explain why an event happened or changed.

related_collocations.example: You can always rely on your best friend.
I was counting on you to bring the cake.
The teacher asked us to focus on the story.

memory_tip: DEPEND + ON = something is controlled by something else (depend on the weather, depend on the time)
